summary: A square brick light on a sandy spit in Seattle's Discovery Park, lit in 1881 and still flashing red and white over Elliott Bay.

notes_for_editor: Much of the narrative rests on LighthouseFriends (facts only, own words). Printed page numbers for the 1894 (p.198), 1895 (p.177) and 1897 reports were inferred from OCR page headers; 1891 report cited by scan page. The 1897 volume entry (892 hours) is taken as fiscal 1897. Shaw drowning is single-source (LighthouseFriends). Newspaper search was not completed. The Bulletin rescue (18 December) is in the January 1916 issue, so it happened in December 1915; LighthouseFriends says 1916. Roster additions are from the USLHS people page (pre-1960 only). Hours of fog-signal operation and stone deliveries are by fiscal year. Conflicts: tower size (NRHP 10 ft sq / 19 ft vs LF 11 ft sq / 21 ft), fog building date, canal year (1915 vs 1917). The record's 7.0 m tower height not verified.
